newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends barely budged, consolidates.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends barely budged, consolidates.

text.p: CSCE world sugar closed little changed after speculative selling stymied an early attempt to rally, floor sources said.
The most-active March contract climbed to 11.35, where a double-bottom formed on the charts last week, but was not able to muster enough interest to reach resistance seen at 11.45.
October ran into resistance at 11.50 but failed to fill a gap on the charts between 11.50 and 11.52.
"Today just looked like a bit of a retracement from the recent selloff," a floor source said.

Market sources said recent speculative liquidation may have pressured the October contract close at its lows. "The specs still have some unwinding to do in October, but open interest has come down to more normal levels following last week's options expiry," a dealer said.
Open interest in October stood at 35,253 lots, off 6,055 lots. Open interest in March rose 2,358 lots to 64,503 lots.

Most-active March closed up 0.02 at 11.30, having ranged from 11.35 to 11.26. Spot-October eased 0.03 on the day to finish at 11.40, barely above the low of 11.40. The back months finished 0.03 to 0.05 higher.

The October/March spread closed at 0.10 compared with 0.15 on Tuesday's close, suggesting further rolling out of October long positions into March. Floor sources agree that the spread is probably at its low.
Tunisia said today it bought 28,000 tonnes of white sugar in two cargoes, for May and July delivery.
LIFFE white sugar futures ended up slightly. December ended up $0.80 at $328.00. Total volume was 2,448 lots.
